why: Unrun detector (982c835 precedent: built and validated against hand-written outcomes only; no paid run has executed it). Bet measured: the LOUD side of the research gate -- the heaviest prose bet in the plugin at ~9,500 words (orch-research-gate.sh 1,693 + orch-signals.sh 1,509 + research-classifier SKILL/STRATEGY/EXAMPLES 2,484 + orch-researcher agent 2,602 + researcher-prompt and research-brief templates 1,216, wc -w). Until now its only behavioral case was research-gate-skips.json, the QUIET side -- so the pipeline could rot into never firing and the suite would stay green. This prompt trips the deterministic sniffer by construction (verified by hand: ORCH_HOOK_DRY_RUN=1 printf '{"prompt":...}' | orch-research-gate.sh -> 'would inject research-gate guidance (signal: design verb + library mention)' -- 'build' is the design verb, 'stripe' the library; 'payment' independently matches the security branch). Correct behavior per the chain hook -> classifier RESEARCH_NEEDED -> orch-researcher -> brief is a dated artifact at docs/llm-orchestrator/research/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>-brief.md whose header carries one of the four first-class Outcome tokens (templates/research-brief.md:4). Deliberately graded on ENGAGEMENT, not fetch success: scratch runs may lack network, so COULDN'T_VERIFY is the honest outcome there and passes -- classifying and attempting is the construct. Check 1 = a well-formed brief with a first-class Outcome line exists; check 2 = that same brief names stripe (a pasted template naming no library passes 1, fails 2). The expect block guards the transcript: must_match 'research' fails the silent-designer, and must_not_match catches the skip phrasings (RESEARCH_SKIP dumped, 'skipping research', 'no research needed'). 'Proceeding on training knowledge' is deliberately NOT in the guard -- it is the honest COULDN'T_VERIFY wording (skills/research-classifier/SKILL.md:82) and must not be punished.

check:
python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import pathlib, re, sys
# Durable evidence that research was ENGAGED: a brief artifact at the path the
# researcher agent is given (docs/llm-orchestrator/research/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>-brief.md,
# agents/orch-researcher.md:21) whose header carries one of the four first-class
# Outcome tokens (templates/research-brief.md:4). Any of the four passes:
# a scratch run without network honestly lands on COULDN'T_VERIFY, and that
# still proves the gate fired and research was attempted.
d = pathlib.Path('docs/llm-orchestrator/research')
if not d.is_dir():
    sys.exit(1)
outcome = re.compile(r"(?mi)^Outcome:\s*(VERIFIED|COULDN.{0,2}T[_ ]?VERIFY|CONTRADICTED|NOT_APPLICABLE)")
for f in sorted(d.glob('*-brief.md')):
    if not re.match(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-.+-brief\.md$', f.name):
        continue
    if outcome.search(f.read_text(errors='replace')):
        sys.exit(0)
sys.exit(1)
PYEOF

python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import pathlib, re, sys
# Anti-boilerplate: the SAME brief that carries a first-class Outcome must name
# the library the prompt committed to (stripe). A template pasted with no
# library fails here while passing check 1.
d = pathlib.Path('docs/llm-orchestrator/research')
if not d.is_dir():
    sys.exit(1)
outcome = re.compile(r"(?mi)^Outcome:\s*(VERIFIED|COULDN.{0,2}T[_ ]?VERIFY|CONTRADICTED|NOT_APPLICABLE)")
for f in sorted(d.glob('*-brief.md')):
    if not re.match(r'\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-.+-brief\.md$', f.name):
        continue
    t = f.read_text(errors='replace')
    if outcome.search(t) and re.search(r'stripe', t, re.I):
        sys.exit(0)
sys.exit(1)
PYEOF
